epistemic_boundary: Donor code is real executable my-lisp/WSM source, but tests in this PR are independent Python models of its observable mathematical laws, not an actual my-lisp/SENS runtime parity proof. Name-level absence is only a prefilter, not behavioral dedup.

candidates.law: Given a finite chain from leaf to root, current per-node (visit_count,value_sum) and a leaf-side exact score v, visit_count increases exactly once at every chain node, value_sum at node depth k from leaf increases (-1)^k*v, and no off-path node changes. The sign changes because each node's score is from its own side-to-move perspective.
candidates.result: same chain identities with updated (visits:int,value_sum:exact-rational) states
falsifiers: Updating a grandparent by -v instead of +v.
Incrementing ancestor visits twice or modifying a sibling.
Treating 0 as a terminal stop before root.
degenerate_cases: A cyclic parent relation is INVALID: do not loop indefinitely.

candidates.law: Given the exact subset of K,Q,k,q before a legal move: moving a white/black king erases both own rights; moving a rook from its home corner erases that right; capturing a rook on its home corner erases that captured side's right; all unrelated rights are preserved. Rights never reappear. This operation updates rights only; it does not itself establish legal move, king safety or FEN validity.
falsifiers: A rook moving from h1 removes white Q as well as K.
A rook captured on a8 leaves black q available.
A rook moving back to h1 re-creates lost K right.
An unrelated pawn move erases some right.
